children.title: Trump declares a national emergency at the southern border
children.description_medium: On January 20, 2025, Trump issued Proclamation 10886, declaring a national emergency at the southern border. The proclamation directed executive agencies to use specified authorities and resources for border enforcement. This action did not itself invoke the Alien Enemies Act. It also set out executive directions.
children.description_long: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump issued Proclamation 10886, declaring a national emergency at the southern border of the United States. The official proclamation directed executive agencies to use specified authorities and resources for border enforcement. It is a discrete action with its own date and stated subject: a national emergency at the southern border. The proclamation did not itself invoke the Alien Enemies Act. The separate invocation of that statute against alleged members of Tren de Aragua came on March 15, nearly two months later, under another presidential proclamation. Keeping the two measures distinct avoids attributing the later statutory action to the January emergency declaration. The supplied GovInfo document is the primary record for the January action and supports its date, title, emergency declaration, and directions to agencies. This account reports the proclamation’s contents without adding claims about the legality or operational effect of authorities beyond what the text documents.
children.date_uncertainty: The date is the date of Proclamation 10886 as published in the official record.

children.title: Trump invokes Alien Enemies Act against alleged Tren de Aragua members
children.description_medium: On March 15, 2025, Trump issued a proclamation invoking the Alien Enemies Act against Venezuelan nationals he alleged were members of Tren de Aragua. The proclamation described the group as engaged in an invasion or predatory incursion; this was separate from the January border emergency. Its own date is March 15.
children.description_long: President Donald Trump issued a proclamation on March 15, 2025, invoking the Alien Enemies Act against Venezuelan nationals whom the administration alleged were members of Tren de Aragua. The proclamation described the group as engaged in an invasion or predatory incursion. The action is separate from Trump’s January 20 declaration of a national emergency at the southern border: that earlier proclamation did not itself invoke the Alien Enemies Act. The White House proclamation is the primary source supplied for the date, the statute invoked, the population to whom the action was directed, and the administration’s characterization of the group. That characterization is presented as the proclamation’s allegation rather than an independently established finding about every person covered. The record supports reporting the invocation as a discrete presidential action on March 15, not as part of the January 20 event. It does not make a separate determination about the legal validity or implementation of the proclamation.
children.date_uncertainty: The date is the date of the White House proclamation invoking the Act.

rationale: The official records support two presidential actions on separate dates. The January border emergency and March Alien Enemies Act invocation are not merged.
